title: Are You 'Most Done?
author: Russell Owen
notes: The Caller's Box 2842, permission: full. The Caller's Box's own notes: "Hey can straighten out as it proceeds. Dance begins with same neighbors as in the hey." **B1's hey is danced by the N2 foursome** (DD27, M8b): on a becket set the four of "on right diagonal, hey" are your couple and the couple across the set one place to your right — the couple the transcript calls N2, which becket's relation table names since M8b joined the ends of the set's own loop up. The hey carries the progression, and the author's note is the check. Measured, that one word is what the dance was waiting for: **closure 60.0000 px became 0.0000 px at every checked length (4-12)**, reach 46.6301 px short became 0.0000 at 4-6 couples and 4.0278-4.6375 at 7 and up, and the `long lines: station "1L" has no line mate` throw that stopped eight of the nine lengths is gone. Q12's fixed diagonal is kept; the straightening drift is not built and the strip does not ask for it. **The hey ends short, and the `~` says so** (M9c). Eight written passes with no `~` are *nine* legs - `legsOfPassList` counts the walk home on top of the last token - so the hey danced 1.125 of the weave instead of 1. The weave's four phases are quarter turns, so an odd multiple of 45 degrees puts every dancer's landing exactly on the bisector between two places and `planSchedule`'s nearest-phase search ties at 45.0000 degrees for all four, which it breaks by list order. The eighth token *is* where a hey for four stops, so `~` is what the record meant. Measured, before -> after, at every checked length: **reach 4.0278-4.6375 px short at 7-12 couples became 0.0000 everywhere**, **`progressed` 51.2250 px became a uniform 40.0000** - one couple place, which is what a becket boundary leaves every body behind by - and the collision at 8, 10 and 12 couples went from 0.000 px to 5.571/5.348. **Still owed, one thing, measured: collision.** At 4 and 6 couples the dance is now **green** (9.900 and 9.413 px). At 5, 7 and 9 it is `0.000 px` at **beat 80**, `c0/lark ~ c2/lark`: two instances of one call settle on places chosen per instance, and nothing de-conflicts the choices across them (`resolve.ts`'s `homesOf` hands both the same pool). At 8, 10 and 12 it is 5.348-5.571 px inside A1, which is the same thing a little further apart. Lisa Greenleaf's alternate B2 (#4700) is in the transcript and is not encoded.
